title: Perioperative management of anticoagulants (warfarin and DOACs)

guidelineVersions: BSH peri-operative anticoagulation guideline (Keeling et al., 2016)
EHRA practical guide on NOACs (Steffel et al., 2021)

related.why: The other common pre-assessment medication plan: diabetes and surgery

brief.scenario: Mr Graham Oakley, 68, is listed for elective laparoscopic cholecystectomy. He takes warfarin for atrial fibrillation (target INR 2.5; CHA2DS2-VASc score 4). His INR today is 2.5.
brief.task: Answer the examiner's questions on planning his anticoagulation around surgery, and on patients taking direct oral anticoagulants (DOACs).

beforeYouWalkIn.frame: Two risks to weigh: clotting off anticoagulation, bleeding from the operation.
beforeYouWalkIn.trap: Bridging every AF patient with a high score. In AF, bridging adds bleeding without preventing strokes.
beforeYouWalkIn.firstMove: "I'd weigh his thrombotic risk against the bleeding risk of the operation."

grid.label: Thrombotic risk and bridging
grid.fail: Plans bridging on the CHA2DS2-VASc score alone.
grid.pass: Asks about stroke or TIA. AF without stroke or TIA in the last 3 months: no bridging.
grid.high: Cites BRIDGE: no bridging was non-inferior for arterial thromboembolism and cut major bleeding by more than half (1.3% v 3.2%).

grid.label: Bleeding risk of the operation
grid.fail: Continues warfarin or treats cholecystectomy as minor.
grid.pass: Classes laparoscopic cholecystectomy as abdominal surgery: high bleeding risk, so anticoagulation must stop.
grid.high: Adds patient factors: antiplatelets, NSAIDs, renal function, previous bleeding.

grid.label: Stopping warfarin
grid.fail: Stops warfarin 1 or 2 days before surgery.
grid.pass: Stops warfarin 5 days before (last dose day -6). INR the day before (oral phytomenadione if 1.5 or more) and on the day of surgery.
grid.high: Emergency reversal: 5 mg IV phytomenadione if surgery can wait 6-8 hours; otherwise four-factor PCC plus IV phytomenadione.

grid.label: Restarting warfarin
grid.fail: Restarts with treatment-dose heparin immediately after surgery.
grid.pass: Restarts warfarin at the usual dose the evening of surgery or next day, if haemostasis is secure.
grid.high: Adds prophylactic-dose LMWH as indicated; full-dose heparin no sooner than 48 hours after high-bleeding-risk surgery.

grid.label: Stopping a DOAC
grid.fail: Stops all DOACs 24 hours before any surgery, or bridges them with heparin.
grid.pass: High bleeding risk: last factor Xa inhibitor dose at least 48 hours before. Dabigatran by creatinine clearance: 48, 72 or 96 hours. No bridging.
grid.high: Uses Cockcroft-Gault creatinine clearance; adds 24 hours if under 50 kg or interacting drugs.

grid.label: Restarting a DOAC
grid.fail: Restarts full-dose DOAC the same evening after cholecystectomy.
grid.pass: After high-bleeding-risk surgery: full dose at 48-72 hours, once haemostasis is secure.
grid.high: Prophylactic-dose LMWH from 6-8 hours after surgery until then; heparin if he cannot take tablets.

grid.label: Recognises high thrombotic risk
grid.fail: Cannot name any patient who might need bridging.
grid.pass: Considers bridging for stroke or TIA within 3 months, VTE within 3 months, or most mechanical valves; involves haematology.
grid.high: Treatment-dose enoxaparin (1.5 mg/kg daily or 1 mg/kg twice daily), last dose at least 24 hours pre-op; questions deferring elective surgery.

grid.label: Written plan
grid.pass: Gives him a written plan with dates for the last dose, INR check and restart; records it in the notes.
grid.high: Includes the discharge plan and informs his GP or anticoagulation clinic.

fail.speaker: examiner
fail.text: How would you assess his thrombotic risk?

fail.speaker: candidate
fail.text: His CHA2DS2-VASc is 4, so he's high risk and needs LMWH bridging.

fail.speaker: examiner
fail.text: Is this a high bleeding risk operation?

fail.speaker: candidate
fail.text: No, it's keyhole. He could probably stay on warfarin.

fail.speaker: candidate
fail.text: Treatment-dose enoxaparin that evening, then warfarin.

fail.speaker: candidate
fail.text: Stop it 24 hours before, and cover with heparin.

fail.speaker: candidate
fail.text: I'm not sure. Anyone with a high score?

fail.speaker: examiner
fail.text: How will he know the plan?

fail.speaker: candidate
fail.text: I'll tell him before he leaves clinic.

pass.speaker: examiner
pass.text: How would you assess his thrombotic risk?

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: Has he had a stroke or TIA? If not in the last 3 months, AF doesn't need bridging.

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: Cholecystectomy is abdominal surgery: high bleeding risk, so warfarin must stop.

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: Last dose six days before, so it's stopped for five days. INR the day before, oral vitamin K if 1.5 or more, and INR again on the day of surgery.

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: Warfarin at his usual dose that evening or the next day, if haemostasis is secure.

pass.speaker: examiner
pass.text: Suppose he took apixaban, creatinine clearance 60.

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: Last dose at least 48 hours before. Dabigatran depends on clearance: 48 hours above 80, 72 hours for 50 to 79, 96 hours for 30 to 49. No bridging.

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: Restart full dose at 48 to 72 hours, once haemostasis is secure.

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: Stroke or TIA within 3 months, VTE within 3 months, or most mechanical valves. I'd involve haematology.

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: I'd give him the plan in writing, with dates, and document it.

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: In BRIDGE, no bridging was non-inferior for arterial thromboembolism and major bleeding fell by more than half, from 3.2% to 1.3%. BSH says AF without a recent stroke or TIA shouldn't be bridged.

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: I'd also ask about antiplatelets, NSAIDs, his renal function and any previous bleeding.

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: If it can wait 6 to 8 hours, 5 mg IV phytomenadione. If not, four-factor PCC 25 to 50 units per kg plus 5 mg IV phytomenadione, then check the INR.

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: Prophylactic LMWH as his VTE assessment indicates. If anyone needed full-dose heparin, not before 48 hours after high-bleeding-risk surgery.

high.speaker: examiner
high.text: How do you judge renal function for a DOAC?

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: Cockcroft-Gault creatinine clearance. I'd add 24 hours if he weighed under 50 kg or took interacting drugs.

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: Until full dose restarts, prophylactic LMWH from 6 to 8 hours after surgery; heparin if he can't take tablets.

high.speaker: examiner
high.text: He had a TIA six weeks ago.

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: Then I'd question operating electively now. If we must, bridge with enoxaparin 1.5 mg/kg daily or 1 mg/kg twice daily, last dose at least 24 hours before.

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: His written plan covers discharge too, and I'd copy it to his GP and anticoagulation clinic.

failures.move: Bridging an AF patient because of a high CHA2DS2-VASc score.
failures.consequence: More major bleeding with no fewer strokes.
INR still raised on the day: cancellation or bleeding.

failures.move: Restarting a full-dose DOAC the same evening after high-bleeding-risk surgery.
failures.consequence: DOACs act within hours, so early full dosing risks haemorrhage.

failures.move: Using one interruption time for every DOAC.
failures.consequence: Dabigatran accumulates in renal impairment; residual anticoagulation at surgery.

recovery.when: You blank on the bridging criteria
recovery.line: In AF I bridge only after a recent stroke or TIA, and I'd discuss that with haematology.

recovery.when: Asked a DOAC time you can't recall
recovery.line: It depends on the drug, renal function and bleeding risk; I'd check the EHRA table.

knowledge.fact: Stop warfarin 5 days before; INR the day before, phytomenadione if 1.5 or more; INR on the day; restart evening of surgery or next day.
AF: bridge only after stroke or TIA within 3 months, or previous stroke or TIA plus three of heart failure, hypertension, age over 75, diabetes.
BRIDGE: no bridging non-inferior for arterial thromboembolism; major bleeding 1.3% versus 3.2%.
High bleeding risk: factor Xa inhibitors at least 48 hours; dabigatran 48, 72, 96 hours for clearance 80 or more, 50-79, 30-49.
Abdominal surgery is high bleeding risk; restart full-dose DOAC at 48-72 hours.
Treatment-dose enoxaparin: 1.5 mg/kg once daily or 1 mg/kg twice daily.

recall.think: Stroke if off too long; bleeding if on.
recall.say: "AF without recent stroke: stop warfarin, no bridging."
do: Ask stroke or TIA in last 3 months

numbers.meaning: factor Xa inhibitor off before high-bleeding-risk surgery

recall.trap: A high CHA2DS2-VASc score alone does not mean bridging.
recall.finish: Restart warfarin that evening or next day; DOAC full dose at 48-72 hours.

sources.name: Keeling D, Tait RC, Watson H; British Committee for Standards in Haematology. Peri-operative management of anticoagulation and antiplatelet therapy. Br J Haematol 2016;175:602-13
sources.supports: Warfarin stopped 5 days before; INR the day before with phytomenadione if 1.5 or more, and on the day; restart evening of surgery or next day at usual dose; Table I bridging criteria (AF: stroke or TIA in last 3 months, or previous stroke or TIA plus three or more of CCF, hypertension, age over 75, diabetes; VTE within 3 months; mechanical valves other than bileaflet aortic without risk factors); AF with CHADS2 4 or less and no stroke or TIA in 3 months should not be bridged (1A); last pre-op LMWH at least 24 hours before; post-op full-dose anticoagulation not before 48 hours after high-bleeding-risk surgery; plan recorded in the notes including discharge; emergency reversal with 5 mg IV phytomenadione if surgery can wait 6-8 hours, otherwise 25-50 u/kg four-factor PCC plus 5 mg IV phytomenadione

sources.name: Douketis JD, Spyropoulos AC, Kaatz S, et al; BRIDGE Investigators. Perioperative bridging anticoagulation in patients with atrial fibrillation. N Engl J Med 2015;373:823-33
sources.supports: No bridging non-inferior to dalteparin bridging for arterial thromboembolism (0.4% vs 0.3%) with less major bleeding (1.3% vs 3.2%); stroke or TIA within 12 weeks excluded

sources.name: Steffel J, Collins R, Antz M, et al. 2021 European Heart Rhythm Association Practical Guide on the use of non-vitamin K antagonist oral anticoagulants in patients with atrial fibrillation. Europace 2021;23:1612-76
sources.supports: Table 12: abdominal surgery is a high bleeding risk intervention; Figure 14: last intake before high-risk surgery at least 48 hours for apixaban, edoxaban and rivaroxaban, and for dabigatran at least 48, 72 and 96 hours for CrCl 80 or more, 50-79 and 30-49 ml/min; no bridging; consider 24 hours longer with weight under 50 kg or interactions; full-dose restart 48-72 hours after high-risk procedures, prophylactic LMWH 6-8 hours post-op in the meantime; written plan for the patient

partner.opening: Mr Oakley is on warfarin for atrial fibrillation and is listed for a laparoscopic cholecystectomy. How would you assess his thrombotic risk?

reveals.trigger: Asks about previous stroke or TIA
reveals.finding: Never had a stroke or TIA.
Hypertension, type 2 diabetes, previous MI. No heart failure.
No antiplatelets or NSAIDs. Creatinine clearance 60 ml/min. No previous bleeding.

reveals.trigger: Asks about the INR the day before surgery

push.question: Does he need bridging?
push.expect: No: AF without a stroke or TIA in the last 3 months.

push.question: What bleeding risk is this operation?
How and when do you stop warfarin?
push.expect: Stop 5 days before; INR the day before; phytomenadione if 1.5 or more; INR on the day of surgery.

push.question: When does warfarin restart?
push.expect: Evening of surgery or next day, usual dose, if haemostasis secure.

push.question: If he took dabigatran, creatinine clearance 60?
push.expect: Last dose at least 72 hours before; no bridging.

push.question: When does a DOAC restart?
push.expect: Full dose at 48-72 hours; prophylactic LMWH in between.

curveballs.prompt: His INR the day before surgery is 1.7.
curveballs.safeAnswer: Give oral phytomenadione and recheck the INR on the morning of surgery.

curveballs.prompt: He had a TIA six weeks ago.
curveballs.safeAnswer: High thrombotic risk: question deferring elective surgery; if not, consider bridging with haematology advice.

curveballs.prompt: He presents instead with perforated cholecystitis needing theatre tonight, INR 2.5.
curveballs.safeAnswer: If surgery can wait 6-8 hours, 5 mg IV phytomenadione; if not, four-factor PCC 25-50 u/kg plus 5 mg IV phytomenadione, then check INR.

curveballs.prompt: He has a mechanical mitral valve instead of AF.
curveballs.safeAnswer: Consider bridging with treatment-dose LMWH; involve haematology and cardiology.
